source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.4
text: Farmers should not keep re-using harvested grain as seed indefinitely: yield and seed quality decline the longer a lot of seed is propagated without renewal from a pure source, because varietal purity degrades and off-types/mixtures accumulate with each successive generation. The manual notes that quality decline becomes noticeable from around the third generation after starting from original (breeder-derived) seed, which is why regular renewal from registered/certified seed sources rather than continuous farmer-saved seed is recommended.

source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.4
text: Using seed of good, verified quality directly determines the yield and quality of the resulting harvest. If the seed used contains a mixture of varieties, this reduces the uniformity and quality of the harvested paddy, which in turn lowers its value and marketability. Producing and using pure, high-quality seed of a known variety is presented as the basis for improving both productivity and farmer income.
